## {.title-slide-de}

<span class="num">PLTW DIGITAL ELECTRONICS · PROJECT 1.2.7</span>

<h1>Understanding digital design: a random number generator</h1>

<p class="meta">Conner Glover · Digital Electronics, Period F · Fall 2026</p>

## One circuit, three sections, one rolling die

::: {.cols style="grid-template-columns: repeat(3, minmax(0, 1fr)); gap: 64px; margin-top: 24px"}
::: {.stack}
<h3>Analog · 555 timer</h3>

An LM555CN makes the clock. A push switch charges a 50 µF capacitor that powers the timer, so the clock runs while the switch is closed and slows to a stop after it opens.
:::

::: {.stack}
<h3>Sequential · counter</h3>

Three 74LS74N D flip-flops count the clock pulses. The count runs 001 to 110 (1 to 6), then resets back to 001.
:::

::: {.stack}
<h3>Combinational · decoder</h3>

Two AND gates, two OR gates and an inverter turn the 3-bit count into the dot pattern of a die face on seven LEDs.
:::
:::

<p class="lede" style="margin-top: 56px">The project: build each section in Multisim, test it on its own, then connect all three. Repeat the build in TinkerCAD.</p>

## Analog section: the 555 clock stops on its own when the roll switch opens

::: {.cols .w46}
<figure class="fig">
<img style="height: 560px; width: auto" src="assets/multisim-555.png" alt="Close-up of the 555 section: switch Key = Space, 1.2 kilohm resistor, 10 kilohm and 18 kilohm timing resistors, 50 microfarad, 100 nanofarad and 10 nanofarad capacitors, LM555CN">
<figcaption><b>Fig 3</b> · The 555 section. The 50 µF and 18 kΩ labels overlap on screen; the values come from the exported netlist.</figcaption>
</figure>

::: {.stack}
<p class="small">The <strong>Space</strong> key toggles switch S1. Closing it charges the 50 µF roll capacitor through 1.2 kΩ. That capacitor feeds RA, so while it's charged the 555 runs as a normal astable clock (RA = 10 kΩ, RB = 18 kΩ, C = 100 nF):</p>

$$f = \frac{1}{0.693\,(R_A + 2R_B)\,C}$$

$$f = \frac{1}{0.693\,(10\,\text{k}\Omega + 36\,\text{k}\Omega)(100\,\text{nF})} \approx 314\ \text{Hz}$$

<div class="readouts">
<div class="readout"><span class="v">3.19<small>ms</small></span><span class="k">calculated period T</span></div>
<div class="readout"><span class="v">60.9<small>%</small></span><span class="k">calculated duty cycle</span></div>
</div>

<p class="small">Opening S1 cuts the charging path. The 50 µF capacitor drains through RA and RB, the timing capacitor charges more and more slowly, and the clock slows down and stops, like a die tumbling to a stop.</p>
:::
:::

## Sequential section: three flip-flops count from 1 to 6

::: {.stack}
<figure class="fig">
<img style="width: 100%; height: auto" src="assets/multisim-sequential.png" alt="Close-up of three 74LS74N D flip-flops across the top of the schematic, with two 74LS08N AND gates and a 74LS04N inverter at the right">
<figcaption><b>Fig 4</b> · The counter: three 74LS74N flip-flops, then the 111 detector (two 74LS08N ANDs and a 74LS04N)</figcaption>
</figure>

::: {.cols style="grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; gap: 64px"}
<p class="small">Each flip-flop has D tied to its own ~Q, so it toggles on every clock edge. The 555 clocks C (the 1s bit), C's ~Q clocks B, and B's ~Q clocks A: a 3-bit ripple counter.</p>

<p class="small">When the count reaches <span class="mono">111</span>, the two AND gates go HIGH and the inverter pulls the async inputs LOW: it clears A and B and presets C. The count jumps back to <span class="mono">001</span>, so it only shows 1–6.</p>
:::
:::

## Combinational section: four equations light seven LEDs

::: {.cols .w64}
::: {.stack}
<figure class="fig">
<img style="width: 100%; height: auto" src="assets/multisim-combinational.png" alt="Close-up of the decoder: 74LS08N and 74LS32N gates, a 74LS04N inverter and seven LEDs with 220 ohm resistors arranged like a die face; the center LED is lit">
<figcaption><b>Fig 5</b> · The decoder and the seven LEDs. In this frame only the center LED (L4) is lit.</figcaption>
</figure>
:::

::: {.stack}
<p class="small">Opposite LEDs always light together, so four signals are enough:</p>

$$L1 = L5 = A + B\cdot C$$

$$L2 = L6 = A \cdot B$$

$$L3 = L7 = A + \overline{C}$$

$$L4 = C$$

<p class="small muted">Read from the exported netlist of my circuit: exactly two AND gates, two OR gates and one inverter. Each LED has a 220 Ω resistor to ground.</p>
:::
:::

## Calculated outputs give the six die faces

<figure class="fig bare" style="margin-top: 40px">
{{< include assets/die-patterns.svg >}}
</figure>

::: {.cols style="grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; gap: 64px; margin-top: 36px"}
<p class="small"><span class="mono">000</span> would light L3 and L7, which looks like a 2. <span class="mono">111</span> would light all seven LEDs, which isn't a die face.</p>

<p class="small">It doesn't matter: the counter goes <span class="mono">001 to 110</span> and resets at <span class="mono">111</span>, so the decoder never sees either one (question 1d).</p>
:::

<p class="caption" style="margin-top: 20px">Expected pattern for each count ABC, worked out from the gate equations · Layout matches the worksheet: L1 L7 top, L2 L4 L6 middle, L3 L5 bottom</p>

## TinkerCAD uses the same clock, counter and decoder design

::: {.cols style="grid-template-columns: repeat(3, minmax(0, 1fr)); gap: 48px"}
::: {.stack}
<h3>Analog · left board</h3>
<img style="height: 280px; width: 100%; object-fit: contain" src="assets/tinkercad-analog.png" alt="555 timer, slide switch, resistors and capacitors on the left breadboard">
<p>The 555 timer, resistors and capacitors form the clock. The slide switch controls the roll circuit.</p>
:::

::: {.stack}
<h3>Sequential · middle board</h3>
<img style="height: 280px; width: 100%; object-fit: contain" src="assets/tinkercad-sequential.png" alt="Two 74HC74 dual D flip-flop packages on the middle breadboard">
<p>Two 74HC74 packages provide the flip-flops for the three-bit counter. The design repeats counts 001 through 110.</p>
:::

::: {.stack}
<h3>Combinational · right board</h3>
<img style="height: 280px; width: 100%; object-fit: contain" src="assets/tinkercad-combinational.png" alt="74HC04 inverter, 74HC08 AND gates, 74HC32 OR gates, seven resistors and seven LEDs">
<p>The 74HC04, 74HC08 and 74HC32 decode the count. Seven resistors limit LED current; seven LEDs form the die face.</p>
:::
:::

<p class="caption" style="margin-top: 26px">TinkerCAD uses 74HC packages; Multisim uses 74LS parts. The supplied GIF now documents the powered circuit. Component values and exact pin connections are not verified by the overview alone.</p>

## The clock sets the speed; the counter and decoder form the die

::: {.cols style="grid-template-columns: repeat(3, minmax(0, 1fr)); gap: 72px; margin-top: 40px"}
<p>The soldered board, Multisim circuit and TinkerCAD build use the same three sections: a 555 clock, a counter and a decoder.</p>

<p>The counter runs hundreds of times a second, far faster than anyone can follow, so where it stops is effectively random, even though the circuit is fully predictable.</p>

<p>The 50 µF roll capacitor is what makes it feel like a real die: the count slows down before it stops instead of freezing instantly.</p>
:::
